item.title: Supreme Court strikes down Trump’s sweeping tariffs
item.description: The Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump's far-reaching global tariffs on Friday, handing him a stinging loss on an issue crucial to his economic agenda.

item.description: IT'S NO surprise that the PLP can throw a good party. The election campaign launch last week was certainly that.

item.title: FNM: Bahamians will bear cost of PLP’s ‘bad deals’ on energy reform
item.description: THE Free National Movement has accused the Davis administration of locking Bahamians into “bad deals” that could push electricity costs as high as 50 to 55 cents per kilowatt-hour and saddle consumers with a recurring $1m monthly burden.

item.title: Power outage ‘played role’ in coach’s death
item.description: THE family of Grand Bahama coach and 2025 Sports Hall of Famer Bonnie Basden believes an island-wide power outage in response to a bomb threat on Thursday morning played a role in her death.

item.title: Court rules ‘redeployment’ of five Family Island Administrators unlawful
item.description: THE government unlawfully moved five Family Island Administrators out of their posts in 2021 by calling the change a “redeployment”, a step the Supreme Court found was, in substance, an unauthorised transfer that had no legal effect.

item.title: Immigration union wants sears fired over ignored grievances
item.description: THE head of the union representing customs and immigration officers has called for Immigration Minister Alfred Sears to be fired, accusing him of ignoring months of complaints over promotions, pay and insurance.

item.title: Heroic worker tackles armed man in brazen robbery
item.description: AN heroic kitchen worker tackled a man armed with a hand-held machine gun during a brazen restaurant robbery in which three British ex-pats had a $20,000 Rolex and a $2,000 gold ring stolen.
